source.quote: Shanling's own announcement for the UA2, read 2026-11-25; the product page /product/396 is 14 image slices and the download page /download/84 offers no PDF, so this is the only source and there is no manual to give the native-DSD sentence its siblings carry. Verbatim: « -ESS ES9038Q2M DAC & Ricore RT6863 amplifier »; « -Hi-Res support up to PCM 32/768 and DSD512 »; « -3.5mm Single ended & 2.5mm Balanced output »; « -Special mode offering compatibility with Nintendo Switch ».

facts.chip: « ESS ES9038Q2M DAC & Ricore RT6863 amplifier ».

_la_source_est_une_annonce_ou_un_manuel_: Shanling's product pages are image-only, so every figure comes from the maker's own announcement at /article/NNNNNN or from its manual PDF, both on en.shanling.com. No number was read off an image, and nothing is sourced to store.shanling.com. See the brand file.
_ni_DoP_ni_natif_ne_sont_dits_pour_ce_mo: DoP appears on no Shanling page or manual, and « native » only in the UA dongle manuals and in EM5. Neither is stated for this model.
_le_seul_UA_sans_manuel_donc_le_seul_san: Every other UA dongle's manual says « Native DSD support up to DSDnnn » in those words, and `native_dsd` is written on all of them. This one has no manual - /download/84 links nothing - so its announcement's « Hi-Res support up to PCM 32/768 and DSD512 » is all there is, and `native_dsd` is ABSENT. Ten dongles of one family, nine of which state their DSD transport and one of which does not, for no reason but a missing file. The figure is the same; the knowledge is not.
